{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7f9bafc8c7d9e7abd580e35e1fb00d557319b1d76402da70d5ae55f2ff9d6641","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Safe driving, intersections and freeways","heading":"C — Safe driving, aggressive driving, intersections, freeways and fatigue","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Safe driving, aggressive driving, intersections, freeways and fatigue

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Safe driving takes more than vehicle basics and memorized rules; it also needs good judgment, reflexes, experience, patience and common sense. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
A teen's skill and confidence grow through practice, first on the driver education range, then with a parent, guardian or designated licensed adult 21 or older, and later alone once licensed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Experienced middle-aged drivers can become complacent, and driving on autopilot leaves them less tuned to the risks around them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Older drivers can improve through added training, and AAA RoadWise Driver and AARP Driver Safety offer refresher courses, listed at Michigan.gov/AgingDriver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Aggressive drivers run stop signs and red lights, speed, tailgate, weave, pass illegally on the right, and may gesture, yell, honk or flash their headlights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Answering aggression in kind can escalate into road rage, where a weapon or the vehicle itself is used to attack another driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Federal highway safety officials have estimated that aggressive driving behaviors cause 66 percent of all traffic fatalities. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Merge smoothly, and when another driver merges or turns badly, slow down, give room, and back off rather than trying to prove you are right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
If someone tailgates you while you pass in the left lane, move back right when safe and let faster traffic go, since a backed-up left lane tempts aggressive drivers to take risks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
If another driver tailgates you, pull over and let them pass so the unsafe driver is ahead where you can see them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
Never gesture at other drivers in anger, and if you made a mistake and someone gestures, signal that you are sorry. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
When confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of the way, avoid eye contact, ignore gestures or insults, and call police to report them when safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A02
If an aggressive driver crashes farther ahead, stop a safe distance from the scene, wait for police and report what you saw. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Intersection crashes cause more traffic deaths and serious injuries than crashes on any other part of the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
Approaching an intersection, check oncoming and cross traffic, pedestrians, signals, signs, markings, road condition and blind areas, and let others go first whenever you are unsure what they will do. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
Look twice for motorcycles, bicycles and mopeds at intersections because their speed and distance are hard to judge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
When trees, buildings or snow piles block your view at an intersection, creep forward slowly until you can see past them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Freeways carry one-direction traffic with no stops or intersections, and pedestrians, motorcycles of 124 cc or less, mopeds, bicycles, ATVs and slow-moving vehicles are banned from them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
Entrance ramps often sit beside exit ramps, so watch for Do Not Enter, Wrong Way and speed limit signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A03
Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speed, signal, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder, then merge into a safe gap, yielding to freeway traffic and not counting on others to let you in. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A03
On a two-lane freeway keep right except to pass, exit left, let a vehicle merge, in heavy congestion, or when emergency vehicles or construction workers are on the shoulders. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A03
With three or more lanes in your direction you may use any lane, but stay with the slower traffic if driving at or near the minimum speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A03
HOV lanes require two or more occupants during peak hours such as rush hour, are open to everyone outside those hours, and motorcycles may use them any time. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
Merge signs near entrances warn of entering traffic; adjust speed or change lanes safely to help them merge, and watch for drivers who brake or swerve suddenly toward an exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Stop on a freeway only in an emergency, and then use hazard flashers, slow gradually and pull completely off the pavement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
Michigan's merge law, MCL 257.649(7), means the merging driver must yield to traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard and adjust speed and position to merge safely, whether entering or leaving the freeway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
To exit, check traffic and signal into the deceleration lane, and do not slow down until you are fully in that lane, then obey the ramp speed limit since many ramps curve sharply. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
If you miss your exit, never back up, turn around or use the median crossover, which is only for emergency and MDOT vehicles; go to the next exit and come back. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Fatigue is one of the biggest freeway dangers, since the steady hum of wind, tires and engine can make you sleepy or hypnotized. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A04
Do not rely on coffee or stay-awake drugs; if tired, take a 10-minute break at least every two hours or let someone else drive. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A04
If you must keep driving while tired, keep moving your eyes across the road, check mirrors, and look near, far, left and right. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A04
Cruise control works best in rural areas with light traffic; set it at or below the speed limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A04
Pressing the accelerator does not cancel cruise control, but pressing the brake pedal does. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A04
Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic, near many ramps, on roads slick with rain, snow or ice, and when towing heavy loads, since constant resetting distracts you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0076]
